title: Western island reclamation will create space for industries, low-carbon energy sources: Analysts
cleaned_text: western island reclamation will create space for industries low-carbon energy sources analysts analysts the new island allow singapore to design from scratch an integrated hub involving a range of low-carbon energy sources that can support jurong island published aug 24 2026 09 35 pm updated aug 25 2026 10 16 am singapore - the reclamation of a new western island will create a space for industries and power-related infrastructure that can tap the sea and benefit from proximity to jurong island and the need for greater distance from residential areas analysts at the national day rally on aug 23 prime minister lawrence wong had outlined plans to form a new island south of energy and chemicals hub jurong island in the coming decades for industry energy and defence needs by merging islands such as pulau semakau pulau bukom and pulau sudong analysts the straits times that the new island allow singapore to design from scratch an integrated hub involving a range of low-carbon energy sources that can support jurong island boosting the nation s long-term energy security by creating space to accommodate technology that become feasible only in the longer term nuclear energy infrastructure is one of the possible options among a host of low-carbon energy sources that can be sited on the island they that they cautioned against seeing the deployment of nuclear energy as the aim of the reclamation stressing that singapore has yet to make a decision on the power source which it is exploring as a low-carbon alternative and noting the need for more detailed studies matthew chew nuclear competency and strategy lead at engineering consultancy hy that the new island give singapore the long-term physical space to accommodate technologies and energy systems that not yet be commercially mature but become critical over the next decades singapore design the island as an integrated energy hub where gas low-carbon fuels electricity imports storage renewables and potentially nuclear eventually operate together he tan-soo jie sheng director of the institute for environment and sustainability at the lee kuan yew school of public policy noted that while western singapore has a large industrial footprint much of that land is already committed to existing uses hence what singapore needs is sufficiently large contiguous sites that can accommodate the new industries and energy infrastructure it need several decades from now he that offshore land provides direct maritime access and space to build large-scale and difficult-to-site energy infrastructure from scratch a common constraint for singapore s energy ambitions tan-soo these characteristics make it particularly suitable for activities that are land- or energy-intensive require port access or benefit from greater physical buffers possibilities include next-generation energy and chemical industries hydrogen- and ammonia-related activities advanced manufacturing and large-scale energy infrastructure sing tien foo nus business school s provost chair professor of real estate the offshore island will prepare singapore for the next wave of industrialisation for which it will need to build a sufficient land bank in advance to attract investment in these greener high-value-add industries he new industries that require massive infrastructure investment are to be segregated from high-density residential housing estates and will require intensive energy and water resources are ideal on the island by isolating these advanced and precision manufacturing risks they protect against other types of human risks including fire and pollution tan-soo noted that fundamentally singapore does not know what the most important industries will be in 2050 or 2070 just as planners of the past did not know the scale of today s demand for data centres and digital infrastructure and the new site offer flexibility he that offshore land provides direct maritime access and the opportunity to build highly specialised infrastructure from scratch in addition the new island potentially helps singapore address a constraint common to several of these pathways by providing sufficient and suitable land for large-scale and difficult-to-site energy infrastructure strategically the move to form a second energy island beside jurong will build resilience for singapore s energy system marsh asia s energy and power leader benjamin chang he singapore s energy security strategy has always been about creating options before you need them chew several factors make the offshore industrial site a candidate for nuclear energy these include access to seawater that can reduce the distance needed to convey water to cool nuclear power plants as well as giving the land-constrained city-state more flexibility without locking up a major parcel on the mainland he citing how nuclear power can represent a commitment of land for potentially 60 years or more analysts that proximity to the singapore armed forces confer greater security but there be trade-offs the colocation of saf on the island enhance security and protect valuable manufacturing plants from potential intrusion by imposing strict controls on access from unrelated parties and by establishing military zones that reduce the risk of sabotage or drone incursions this mirrors the existing model on jurong island where strict access controls and security protocols protect high-value petrochemical and energy facilities saf proximity reinforce the new island s role as a secure strategic node for singapore s future energy system sing chu jian a professor at ntu and its president s chair in civil engineering pointed out that while the military runway on pulau sudong make the future development much easier to plan there be restrictions on construction activities such as height controls experts cautioned that use of the reclaimed island mean navigating complex hurdles such as sea-level rise emergency access and environmental impacts given its scale nus energy studies institute senior research fellow kim jeong won significant investment be needed for land reclamation transport links utility networks and grid connections potentially making offshore generation more expensive than developing existing sites

title: PSI or PM2.5? What air quality measures should I refer to when there is haze?
cleaned_text: psi or pm2 5 what air quality measures should i refer to when there is haze a hazy city skyline as seen from gardens by the bay at 4 50pm on aug 24 published aug 24 2026 09 10 pm updated aug 25 2026 10 14 am singapore - the spectre of haze loomed over singapore on aug 24 as the pollutant standards index psi in the central region inched ever closer to unhealthy levels the 24-hour psi reading was 98 at 9pm just shy of 101 which indicates unhealthy air for weeks sumatra and kalimantan have been ablaze with forest and land fires fuelled by a super el nino how badly singapore is affected hinges on wind direction the straits times explains how local air quality readings should be used to plan outdoor activities haze and worsening air quality are shown through two readings on the national environment agency s nea website the 24-hour pollutant standards index psi and the one-hour pm2 5 readings both measures serve different functions during hazy periods the one-hour pm2 5 an indicator of fine micro-pollutants in the air is what you should be watching because it points to current air quality pm2 5 levels should be checked immediately before outdoor activities such as going jogging or walking your dog pm2 5 refers to micro-pollutants found in smoke haze from indonesian forest fires these particles 30 times smaller than the width of a strand of hair can get lodged deep in the lungs and enter the bloodstream on the afternoon of aug 24 the one-hour pm2 5 readings reached elevated levels in the central and east regions at 56ug m3 and above pm2 5 values can be volatile and tend to fluctuate over the day especially during haze pm2 5 is the dominant pollutant during periods of transboundary haze and has the most influence over the 24-hour psi readings the 24-hour psi is computed based on the daily average concentration of six pollutants including pm2 5 sulphur dioxide carbon monoxide and ozone the calculations are done based on readings from the past 24 hours it is an index to provide easily understandable information about daily levels of air quality haze has descended when the psi crosses 100 reaching unhealthy levels during a haze episode the national environment agency will issue a third air quality measure called the 24-hour psi forecast not to be confused with the 24-hour psi the psi forecast indicates what the air quality is expected to be in the next 24 hours and can be used to plan activities ahead of time in a nutshell during haze people should refer to the pm2 5 values if they want to go outdoors within the hour and refer to the psi forecast if they are planning an outdoor activity the next day during haze if the pm2 5 readings are high between 151ug m3 and 250ug m3 people should avoid strenuous outdoor activities for the next hour vulnerable people who include seniors pregnant women children and patients with lung and heart disease should avoid all outdoor activities these are outlined in the personal guide published on nea s website hazy conditions seen from ang mo kio facing eastern singapore on aug 24 n95 masks are not needed for short periods of exposure such as commuting to work these masks are recommended under certain conditions such as when a healthy person must be outdoors for several hours when the air quality is in the hazardous range with a psi reading of over 300 the authorities have that national n95 mask stockpiles are sufficient when the outdoor air quality appears to be worsening close doors and windows if the air-conditioner draws in unfiltered air from outside close the outdoor air intake opening portable air purifiers can be used to further improve indoor air when planning for outdoor activities the next day refer to the 24-hour psi forecast and accompanying health advisory when air quality is forecast to remain unhealthy at 101 and above healthy individuals should reduce prolonged and strenuous outdoor activities seniors pregnant women and children should minimise prolonged outdoor exertion and those with lung and heart disease should avoid such activities for healthy folk continuous exposure to unhealthy air over a few days cause eye nose and throat irritation they will resolve on their own in most cases a hazy jurong east skyline at 5 53pm on aug 24 lee joon loong medical director of paddington medical clinic reminds patients with asthma to keep their reliever inhalers readily available and ensure that their inhalers are not expired and are being used correctly similarly patients with hay fever should make sure that their antihistamines or nasal sprays are readily available and use them if their symptoms flare up patients should seek medical review early if their symptoms are worsening rather than waiting until they become severely breathless lee shabana begum is a correspondent with a focus on environment and science at the straits times
environment_keywords: haze pm2, psi readings, singapore affected, hours index, unhealthy levels

title: Dung beetles bring poo-sitive news about animals in Central Catchment Nature Reserve
cleaned_text: dung beetles bring poo-sitive news about animals in central catchment nature reserve ntu research fellow ong xin rui left and associate professor eleanor slade with specimens of local dung beetles there are more than 25 known local dung beetle species in singapore published aug 24 2026 05 00 am updated aug 25 2026 01 50 pm singapore deep in the central catchment nature reserve shiny black beetles roll animal dung for their food and nests and some navigate with the light of the milky way new research has proven that dung beetles not only help to break down animal faeces but that their unusual diet can give clues about the elusive mammals and birds that roam the forests these tiny but mighty insects can help to fortify biodiversity surveys that currently rely on camera traps and assess the health of forests between january and march 2023 an ntu team led by associate professor eleanor slade and research fellow ong xin rui placed 100 traps made of plastic bottles and disposable plates on the forest floor and canopies across 50 sites in the central catchment nature reserve singapore s largest green lung ong xin rui left and eleanor slade preparing a trap using plastic bottles and disposable plates at one of the 50 sites of the central catchment nature reserve slade is holding bait made of human faeces wrapped in a thin cloth to attract dung beetles to the trap to lure scuttling dung beetles into the traps the scientists placed a bundle of human faeces wrapped in cloth at each trap harnessing their strong sense of smell dung beetles are particularly drawn to human waste each trap was left in the field for 24 hours before the researchers returned to collect the beetles tropical dung beetles typically move around 100m a day stopping to slurp nutrients inside animal droppings a trap with a plastic bottle dug into the soil to catch dung beetles and a disposable plate overhead the bait hangs under the plate to lure the beetles slade who heads the tropical ecology and entomology lab at ntu s asian school of the environment the dung beetles will have been flying around and eating dung that s in the forest and we re just using the bait to draw them in and then they land but their guts are full from what they ve been eating previously their stomachs contain a mush of mammal and avian dna that the scientists sought to identify ong the main objective of this study was to draw the interactions between the dung beetles and the types of vertebrate or mammal dung they were feeding on more than 540 dung beetles belonging to 14 species were trapped over two months with the contents of their guts analysed in the lab a dung beetle from the group catharsius found in the central catchment nature reserve the team estimates that there are around 25 dung beetle species in singapore including those that are new to science after dissecting the beetles ong and her team separated the half-digested materials from their stomachs and transferred them inside solutions that amplify the dna of mammals and vertebrates such as birds and frogs after dissecting the beetle its gut contents are separated for processing and dna analysis the samples were sent to a company that sequenced or mapped the dna found in the beetles guts a total of 18 animal species were detected through dna matching including the elusive sambar deer sunda pangolin and sunda slow loris other wildlife detected include the brahminy kite a bird of prey and a few squirrel and frog species such as the black-eyed litter frog as part of the processing the contents of the beetle s gut are transferred to a solution that extracts the dna ong noted the ones that jumped out to me were the two frog species you think dung beetles feed on the waste of a python or a monitor lizard not a frog but there are species of dung beetles that feed on carcasses or the beetle have fed on something that ate a frog she highlighted how the study can map food webs the research findings were published in scientific journal molecular ecology resources while the central catchment nature reserve is known to be rich in biodiversity the study was exciting for the ntu researchers because they demonstrated that dung beetles can be used as a dna resource for surveying wildlife in tropical forests while such biodiversity surveys are commonly done through camera traps the cameras are usually placed on the forest floor which miss wildlife residing in the canopy it be difficult to identify the specific species of forest rodents through a camera and having specific dna sequences helps noted ong who is a researcher at the nus lee kong chian natural history museum beyond just documenting the types of animals in the forest the researchers were able to map the interactions between dung beetles and animals across the forest sites slade what happens if you lose some species is the resilience in there the next step in ecological research for conservation is to look just beyond counting species to actually looking at how they interact and that s not been done a lot in the tropics these efforts can help to measure the ecological value of a forested area that is planned for development or track how a degraded forest is improving through conservation projects she moving forward the team is looking to test another way of extracting mammals dna from dung beetles without dissecting them they plan to swab the beetles surfaces such as the mouths and bodies which potentially contain traces of wildlife dna before sending the swabs for dna analysis ash welch a nature-based solutions and biodiversity specialist at infrastructure consultancy aecom the ntu research shows the effectiveness of emerging sampling techniques giving consultants the grounding to adopt them alongside traditional survey methods in environmental assessments what tends to be lacking is an in-depth understanding of ecological networks and the interactions that occur within an ecosystem he knowing about these is important he because ecosystems can provide benefits such as urban cooling against heat and soak up planet-warming greenhouse gases that matters because a species list tells you only what is present a network tells you whether the system is actually working welch while the research is clear using dung beetles for surveys needs to be adopted by frameworks that govern environmental impact assessments he shabana begum is a correspondent with a focus on environment and science at the straits times
environment_keywords: beetles traps, tropical dung, extracting mammals, reserve singapore, catchment nature

title: Train and bus users will have reminders to keep Singapore clean in Public Hygiene Council campaign
cleaned_text: train and bus users will have reminders to keep singapore clean in public hygiene council campaign participants at asean u n i t e on aug 23 discarding trash after the event published aug 23 2026 01 55 pm updated aug 26 2026 02 45 pm singapore public transport users will be reminded to help keep singapore clean as part of the public hygiene council s phc 2026 campaign a keep singapore clean-themed train on the north east line will be launched in september decals covering the interior of all train cars will carry messages encouraging everyone to play his or her role to keep the country clean public transport was chosen as the avenue for the new campaign due to the high footfall it receives daily phc s executive director christina liew who made the announcement on aug 23 later in 2026 the messages will be carried on 10 public buses plying different routes across singapore so every day whether it s the young or old or anybody in between it will reach everyone who takes public transport liew she was speaking at the second asean u n i t e you and i together everytime held at punggol coast digital village asean u n i t e is phc s initiative that brings together diverse communities residing in singapore while promoting environmental stewardship through clean and sustainable practices the event on aug 23 saw over 400 participants from brunei darussalam cambodia myanmar philippines thailand and timor-leste taking part in a community clean-up and cultural performances ambassadors from those countries at the event were present as environmental advocates to amplify the cleanliness message within their respective communities the keep singapore clean 2026 campaign was launched in april with a 30-second video screened across malls reminding shoppers to bin takeaway cups and dispose of food packaging to mark phc s 15th anniversary it organised a roving exhibition with interactive stations tracing its history and launched the cleanliness champions relay where 20 schools and companies took turns to organise clean-up activities around singapore the first leg of the relay was held at kent ridge park on april 19 with subsequent activities planned in areas including newton choa chu kang sengkang west coast park and east coast park in phc launched a community wall mural at little india mrt station made up of photos of phc s partners from town councils and grassroots organisations as part of the keep singapore clean campaign addressing the attendees at the aug 23 event senior parliamentary secretary for sustainability and the environment goh hanyan good public hygiene and cleanliness is key to building a cleaner healthier and more liveable environment an example of this was how members of the public returned their food trays and properly disposed of rubbish during the covid-19 pandemic first-time phc volunteer iveca cale villalon ignacio echoed similar views the 35-year-old who has been working as a nurse in singapore for the past decade she became a volunteer with phc as public hygiene is an important issue to her ignacio who performed two songs at the event she was open to participating in more clean-up activities in the future as a healthcare worker i m very interested in infection control and public hygiene if there s no public hygiene we have more patients in the hospital

title: Tuas Power to build hydrogen-ready power plant by 2031
cleaned_text: tuas power to build hydrogen-ready power plant by 2031 the energy regulator forecasts that singapore s peak electricity demand is expected to grow by between 2 4 per cent and 4 8 per cent annually over the next 10 years published aug 20 2026 05 00 pm updated aug 21 2026 02 17 pm singapore a hydrogen-ready natural gas power plant to be built by local electricity generator tuas power is slated to begin operations in 2031 the combined cycle gas turbine ccgt facility which will be housed in tuas power station will have a capacity of 670mw enough to power up to about 1 2 million four-room flats a year the plant can burn up to 30 per cent hydrogen a cleaner fuel with natural gas making up the rest to generate electricity it can use diesel as a back-up fuel when needed the energy market authority ema announced on aug 20 that tuas power had won the right to build own and operate a new ccgt generating unit this came after the authority in april called for energy companies to build up to three new hydrogen-compatible power plants in 2031 and 2032 to help meet singapore s future electricity needs with this award there will be at least 11 hydrogen-ready natural gas power plants in singapore by 2032 including four that were completed in 2025 tuas power on aug 20 that the new plant will not only help to meet singapore s growing electricity demand but replace ageing generators that are due to retire over the next decade the plant is scheduled to start operating by december 2031 it when asked about the cost of the facility tuas power s chief operating officer michael wong that the industry benchmark for such a facility is between 700 million and 1 billion the final cost will be subject to tender outcomes from 2024 all new and repowered natural gas power plants need to be 10 per cent more efficient and be able to draw on at least 30 per cent hydrogen when the low-carbon energy source becomes viable in the future hydrogen is considered a clean fuel as it does not produce any co2 when burned natural gas on the other hand is a fossil fuel singapore s electricity demand is expected to grow rapidly over the next several years driven by strong economic growth and transport electrification as well as the expansion of energy-intensive sectors such as semiconductor manufacturing and data centres ema in a statement the energy regulator forecasts that singapore s peak electricity demand is expected to grow by between 2 4 per cent and 4 8 per cent annually over the next 10 years peak demand refers to the highest amount of electricity used in a specific period much like the rush hour of power used by 2031 the peak demand is projected to reach between 9 6 gigawatt gw and 11 4 gw singapore s peak demand in 2025 was around 8gw the call for new power plants in april came after four back-up power units were completed in 2025 known as fast-start plants they are designed to kick-start within minutes if there is a sudden shortfall in power supply electricity retailer pacificlight power completed its two 50mw back-up units in june 2025 and ema subsidiary meranti power launched its two 340mw fast-start units in october 2025 keppel launched its 600mw hydrogen-compatible plant in while sembcorp is expected to launch its 600mw hydrogen-compatible plant in 2026 ytl powerseraya is slated to build its 600mw hydrogen-compatible plant by 2027 followed by pacificlight power s 670mw facility which is scheduled for 2029 chin hui shan is a journalist covering the environment beat at the straits times

title: Disasters know no borders; climate change escalation requires shared ASEAN response: Edwin Tong
cleaned_text: disasters know no borders climate change escalation requires shared asean response edwin tong minister for law and second minister for home affairs edwin tong speaking at the asean strategic policy dialogue on disaster management 2026 on aug 19 published aug 19 2026 10 50 am updated aug 19 2026 09 09 pm singapore climate change is intensifying the frequency and severity of natural disasters and building resilience is no longer optional minister for law and second minister for home affairs edwin tong he that such disasters know no borders making solidarity and collective action in asean critical tong was speaking at the asean strategic policy dialogue on disaster management 2026 held at parkroyal collection marina bay on aug 19 the 11th edition of the event was co-organised by the singapore civil defence force the asean secretariat and the asean coordinating centre for humanitarian assistance on disaster management the event saw some 200 government officials academics and practitioners present including representatives from asean countries the european union canada and new zealand in his opening speech tong 2026 marked the 10th anniversary of the one asean one response declaration he the declaration had set out a clear ambition to increase the speed scale and solidarity of asean s response to any disaster recognising that an effective response cannot rest on any single institution or mechanism alone he yet even as we have strengthened our capabilities the challenges we face have grown they ve in fact intensified natural disasters have worsened in both scale as well as frequency and in many ways its unpredictability at the start of his speech tong extended his condolences to indonesia which experienced a 7 7-magnitude earthquake off the coast of flores island on aug 15 thousands have been displaced and at least 53 people were killed rescue efforts are ongoing attendees at the dialogue observed a moment of silence for the victims of the disaster during a speech by raditya jati indonesia s deputy minister for systems and strategy at the national disaster management authority tong extended his condolences to the philippines which is experiencing the compound effect of tropical cyclones luis and maymay and the south-west monsoons other asean countries have not been spared tong the earthquake that struck mandalay in myanmar on march 28 2025 was one of the deadliest disasters of the year affecting thailand and vietnam as well he mentioned cyclone senyar which brought widespread devastation across indonesia thailand and malaysia a key concern is the warning earlier in 2026 by the world meteorological organization of a super el nino tong this mean more severe heatwaves and droughts with serious consequences for food security and public health in south-east asia he these events remind us that natural disasters do not at all respect national boundaries national borders they are regional challenges that demand regional solutions as climate change continues to intensify the frequency and severity of natural disasters across our region and elsewhere in the world building resilience and depth is no longer optional in fact i believe it is an imperative it is a must-do tong singapore will take up the asean chairmanship in 2027 and it intends to deepen collective preparedness and resilience on several fronts this includes the hosting of the 10th asean regional disaster emergency response simulation exercise which will test and validate regional disaster response procedures and coordination singapore will advance asean s climate and environmental agenda having designated 2026 as the year of climate adaptation and is developing a national adaptation plan underpinned by a 40 million commitment to create a climate-ready nation tong that beyond preparedness collective action is essential and can be extended beyond asean he we must move beyond reactive responses alone and embed anticipatory thinking into the foundations into the very core of our approach to disaster management i believe that asean is well-placed to build on its strong foundations to advance the implementation of one asean one response initiatives and eventually extend our collective capabilities to the broader international community david sun is the straits times crime correspondent he has a background in criminology and is a licensed private investigator humanitarian aid disaster relief

title: 76% of coral reefs in Indo-Pacific at risk of drowning from rising seas in coming decades: NTU study
cleaned_text: 76 of coral reefs in indo-pacific at risk of drowning from rising seas in coming decades ntu study coral reefs from the indo-pacific most corals will not be able to keep pace with the waters if sea level rise exceeds 5 3mm per year a threshold that can be surpassed by the 2060s if greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise rapidly published aug 18 2026 06 45 pm updated aug 21 2026 02 18 pm singapore three-quarters of coral reefs in the indo-pacific region which includes singapore drown as sea levels rise a study by nanyang technological university ntu has found most corals will not be able to keep pace with the waters if sea level rise exceeds 5 3mm per year a threshold that can be surpassed by the 2060s if greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise rapidly as at 2023 global sea level rise had been around 4 5mm per year to nasa as riovie ramos the study s first author and research fellow at ntu s earth observatory of singapore put it rising sea level is not the first enemy of coral reefs longer-term sea level rise compounds the threats the underwater gardens already face because of construction works at coastal areas and bleaching caused by marine heatwaves the loss of complex reef structures reduce the habitats available to fish although coral reefs are submerged if sea levels rise faster than a reef s growth the reef will sit under progressively deeper water a process scientists call reef drowning deeper waters tend to cut off sunlight and the survival of corals is highly dependent on the amount of light available in singapore corals already live in murky waters and any further reduction in light reaching them can be dangerous the loss of complex reef structures reduce the habitats available to fish and other marine animals affecting fisheries tourism and communities that depend on reefs for food and income ntu in a statement on aug 18 kyle morgan an assistant professor at ntu s asian school of the environment who led the research reefs will become progressively submerged they still contain living corals but they will no longer function in the same way potentially allowing greater wave energy to reach the coastline and increasing flood risks to coastal communities the study was done by tracing the histories of 288 ancient reef cores from 92 sites across the indo-pacific including the great barrier reef in australia maldives and the coral triangle one of the most biodiverse marine areas in the world spanning the waters of south-east asia and the solomon islands reef cores are metres-long cylinders of rock drilled from the reef base made up of calcium carbonate they preserve entire past coral histories by calculating the dates of different sections of a core scientists can reconstruct how reefs have built up over thousands of years and how the types of corals living on them have changed through time the ntu researchers calculated the coral fossils vertical growth rate across 11 700 years which is the current geological era after the last ice age these were done by scouring existing research and by studying some cores collected by the researchers assistant professor kyle morgan and research fellow riovie ramos examining a reef core reef cores from singapore were not included in the study to make future projections the researchers identified the highest growth rate each reef achieved in the past and compared them to future sea level rise scenarios ramos under the high-emissions scenario the sea is projected to rise faster than 76 per cent of the studied reefs can grow meaning they will likely be inundated by 2100 ramos thousands of years ago during the early holocene period reefs were often in a high growth state allowing them to keep up with sea level rise today reefs face repeated bleaching ocean acidification pollution and other stressors which reduce their ability to produce carbonate materials needed for vertical growth she noted the study s findings were published in scientific journal nature communications in august the researchers found that the changing landscape of coral reefs with an increasing share of weedy species speed up reef drowning weedy species are small fast-growing corals that can settle on disturbed reefs but are poor at growing upwards at 1 9mm a year weedy species are just like weeds on land they grow fast and cover reef quickly but don t provide meaningful structure or habitat morgan ancient reefs on the other hand were made up of competitive branching corals that grew upwards the fastest at 4mm a year conservation and reef restoration efforts cannot fully compensate for coral loss if sea levels continue accelerating ntu a 2023 study led by nus marine biologist huang danwei found that in a high carbon emissions scenario up to 10 per cent of singapore s corals perish these dead corals will not be able to contribute to future reef growth and thus further impact coral reef persistence over the next century huang an associate professor and deputy head of the nus lee kong chian natural history museum commenting on the ntu study he conservation efforts must be tailored to local reef conditions which include water quality and the movement of water and sediments stressing that the water quality of reefs should be improved he allowing reefs to naturally recruit landward as sea levels rise reduce the overall loss of reef habitats unless emissions are meaningfully curbed and coral reefs actively managed the processes that build coral reefs and the vital ecosystem services they provide will remain in jeopardy shabana title: askST: How worrying is Singapore’s haze outlook, and how can you protect yourself?
cleaned_text: askst how worrying is singapore s haze outlook and how can you protect yourself firefighters battling a spreading peat fire in a residential district in pengerang johor in january published aug 10 2026 06 25 pm updated aug 11 2026 12 40 pm singapore dry conditions that have worsened fires in the region are expected to persist this week raising the risk of haze over singapore on aug 9 the republic s haze task force announced its readiness to roll out plans after the 24-hour pollutant standards index psi entered the moderate range in central singapore in the afternoon following the recent warning of the possible return of hazy weather the straits times looks at what residents need to know to protect themselves singapore is among the southern south-east asian countries at high risk of severe haze affecting the region for the rest of 2026 these conditions are expected to peak from august to september to think-tank singapore institute of international affairs this is due to unusually hot and dry weather fuelled by an intensifying el nino climate phenomenon el nino occurs when the atmosphere reacts to a sustained warming of the pacific ocean s surface temperatures above average levels bringing less rain longer dry spells and higher temperatures to south-east asia scientists have warned that the 2026 2027 el nino become a godzilla or super el nino with temperatures in the tropical pacific warming rapidly el nino events tend to have the greatest bearing on singapore s rainfall during the dry south-west monsoon season from june to september past moderate-to-strong el nino events over the last 30 years have resulted in 40 per cent to 80 per cent less rainfall in parts of singapore for some months these drier and warmer conditions worsen the region s peatland and forest fires which are the main drivers for transboundary haze experienced in singapore the national environment agency nea on aug 9 the dry conditions that escalated hot spots in indonesia s sumatra and kalimantan are expected to persist in the coming week increasing the risk of haze if the fires persist under prevailing southeasterly winds smoke haze be carried to singapore especially from the hot spots in the southern parts of sumatra for 2026 the confluence of el nino and the potential development of another climate phenomenon called the positive indian ocean dipole prolong the dry season and extend it into october a positive indian ocean dipole is similar to el nino but develops in the equatorial indian ocean to manage the impact of haze singapore set up a task force in 1994 chaired by nea the task force which typically convenes yearly before the dry season starts in june has already met twice in 2026 the task force will roll out its plans air quality enters the unhealthy range when th e 24-hour psi derived from the 24-hour average concentration levels of six pollutants exceeds 100 once the psi enters the unhealthy zone between 101 and 200 nea will issue daily haze advisories to help the public plan their activities for the following day in such conditions the elderly pregnant women and children are advised to minimise prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical activities people with chronic lung and heart diseases should avoid such activities entirely should air quality exceed certain thresholds outdoor events can be cancelled and schools closed for example when the psi soared to the very unhealthy range in 2015 primary and secondary schools special education schools and kindergartens run by the ministry of education were closed for a day an acrid burning smell often accompanies transboundary haze due to a mixture of gases from forest and peat fires these pungent gases are different from the air pollutants monitored for air quality the smell tends to be worse at night when winds are weaker slowing the dilution and dispersal of pollutants cooler temperatures restrict their upward dispersal poor visibility does not necessarily mean the air is more polluted lower visibility can be due to the amount of water vapour in the air as water droplets scatter light certain air pollutant particles attract water molecules creating larger particles that scatter even more light this means visibility can be much lower on hazy days with high humidity or rain occasionally the smell of burning can be due to localised burning rather than transboundary haze monitor the one-hour pm2 5 readings which are a key indicator of current air quality during transboundary haze periods these readings reflect the average concentration of fine particulate matter over the past hour and can fluctuate throughout the day based on weather conditions there are four bands on the pm2 5 concentration scale zero to 55 for normal 56 to 150 for elevated 151 to 250 for high and very high for any higher reading when these readings are at elevated levels vulnerable individuals including the elderly pregnant women and those with chronic lung or heart disease should avoid all outdoor activities for the next hour the public can view a personal guide for planning outdoor activities using these readings at this website n95 masks are not needed for short periods of exposure such as commuting to work or walking from a bus stop to a shopping centre these masks are recommended under certain conditions such as if a healthy person must be outdoors for several hours when the air quality is in the hazardous range with a psi reading of over 300 surgical masks can reduce discomfort caused by haze by acting as a barrier against larger irritant particles but unlike n95 masks they are not effective in filtering fine particles to stay updated check the nea website nea gov sg the haze microsite haze gov sg the myenv app and the nea s social media channels for the latest information residents can protect their indoor environment by closing doors and windows to limit haze particles entering the home wet-cleaning methods such as mopping and wiping can be used to remove settled dust those with air-conditioners that draw unfiltered air from the outside should ensure outdoor air intake openings are closed portable air purifiers can help cut indoor particle levels opt for purifiers equipped with highly efficient air filters to remove fine particles more tips can be found at this website the authorities national n95 mask stockpiles are sufficient during one of singapore s worst episodes of haze pollution in 2015 vulnerable and needy singaporeans were able to collect n95 masks from community clubs islandwide meteorological service singapore

title: Air-con not needed to cool a building
cleaned_text: air-con not needed to cool a building office development paya lebar green is one of 50 buildings in singapore that rely on alternative cooling methods instead of air-conditioning published aug 10 2026 05 00 am updated aug 21 2026 02 19 pm singapore hotter days on the horizon are set to stretch demand for cooling indoors air -conditioning is an energy guzzler that contributes to global warming when it emits planet-warming refrigerants cooling alone accounts for 40 per cent to 60 per cent of a commercial building s total energy use in singapore nearly 50 buildings in singapore have adopted alternative cooling methods that safeguard workers comfort while reducing energy use alternative cooling technologies that do not rely solely on air-conditioning can reduce a building s energy use for cooling by up to 48 per cent air-conditioning set at a higher temperature between 25 5 deg c and 27 deg c is paired with fans fans increase air movement which helps the body release heat more easily through the skin hybrid cooling is the most widely used alternative cooling method as there is no need for major retrofits to date 26 buildings have adopted this including the gear kajima corp s regional headquarters and temasek shophouse the gear uses a mix of methods including hybrid cooling natural ventilation and radiant cooling to achieve a 45 per cent reduction in energy use for cooling a room can be cooled through panels on its ceiling heat naturally moves from warmer objects to cooler surfaces this system removes heat by circulating chilled water through panels pipes or surfaces absorbing heat and keeping temperatures of surfaces below room temperature a network of pipes carrying chilled water draws heat away to cool the building via radiation and natural convective air movement radiant cooling panels attached to a ceiling within the gear cooling and ventilation are provided through ceiling-mounted systems called active chilled beams each beam contains coils that carry chilled water fresh air that has been cooled and treated is pushed through small nozzles in the beam this fast-moving airflow draws warmer air in the room across the cold water coils cooling it down before the air sinks to reach people in the room active chilled beams far left top at l-acoustics office in paya lebar green a study that the building and construction authority commissioned in 2024 identified that these newer cooling technologies can help high-performing green buildings save up to 80 per cent of their energy use up from 72 per cent now this last-mile gap of 8 percentage points calls for technologies that are more novel in nature or require higher upfront investments planning and design following the study upcoming office tower the clifford at raffles place will be piloting another cooling method for the building s retail space this method is called passive displacement cooling which involves leveraging the natural rise of warm air cooling coils near the ceiling will cool the warm air which then sinks to the floor this creates a continuous cycle this marks the first time such cooling technology is being tested for a retail environment in singapore it is more common in office and classrooms elsewhere

title: Sunda slow loris found in industrial estate near Tuas released after 2 months
cleaned_text: sunda slow loris found in industrial estate near tuas released after 2 months a sunda slow loris was rescued by the animal concerns research and education society from an industrial estate in western singapore on 26 published aug 09 2026 05 00 am updated aug 10 2026 05 47 am singapore workers were surprised to discover a young slow loris peering at them inside an industrial building near tuas in the fuzzy creature was eventually rescued by the animal concerns research and education society acres which identified it as the sunda slow loris an endangered venomous primate native to singapore this has been the second sunda slow loris rescued by acres so far in 2026 the first was found in the corridor of an hdb block in sin ming in january the case was unusual as the species wild population is confined to the central catchment nature reserve acres chief executive kalaivanan balakrishnan adding that the slow loris was first spotted on a tree before it entered the premises he guessed that the tree-dwelling primate have accidentally hitched a lift in a lorry or was an abandoned illegal pet the sunda slow loris rescued in was rehabilitated for two months at the acres wildlife rescue centre in jalan lekar fortunately the animal was only mildly dehydrated upon discovery kalaivanan declined to reveal further details about its location due to the species rarity and its popularity in the illegal wildlife trade slow lorises are prominent in the illegal wildlife trade they are sadly mistreated and used as photo props in other countries he it is rare to come across cases involving wild slow lorises due to their shy and elusive nature acres wildlife rescue and rehabilitation manager karina lim however lim as more habitat loss occurs it result in animals venturing out in search of other suitable green spaces to inhabit notwithstanding the slow loris mysterious origins it was deemed suitable for release as it did not display any captive behaviours or physical modifications common among illegally kept pets with bulbous eyes and furry bodies these slow-moving primates look like stuffed toys but their venom-filled bites can rot flesh and cause anaphylactic shock in humans in the exotic pet trade poachers typically cut or pull out the animal s sharp teeth to prevent it from biting its owner to prepare for the slow loris release a customised rehabilitation plan was developed from reviewing scientific literature and consulting an overseas wildlife rescue organisation with expertise in slow lorises lim the nocturnal animal was monitored almost nightly and fed a diet including insects bird eggs and tree sap much of which had to be sourced naturally she fluid was given to resolve signs of stress detected in its blood possibly the result of being stranded outside of its natural environment acres veterinary department manager tan hui min once the staff saw that the slow loris climb forage and demonstrate a healthy aversion to humans they knew that it was time to goodbye the sunda slow loris before it was released in august into a forested area inhabited by wild slow lorises lim we have been rooting for his release from the very start and we are glad that after two months of rehabilitation efforts he was able to return and be free in the wild again on aug 3 the primate was released in a forested area populated by fellow wild slow lorises as singapore continues to clear its forested areas for developments acres is looking to help wildlife and improve their welfare kalaivanan with expansion plans taking shape at acres we are able to do a lot more advanced rehabilitation work which will give both our native and non-native wild animals a better chance back in the wild he the sunda slow loris is the only known venomous primate it produces a yellow secretion from glands on its inner arm which combines with saliva to deliver a painful bite due to illegal demand for slow lorises as pets all nine o f its species are currently threatened with extinction

as a key economic pillar as the nation continues its pursuit of clean energy announcing the change on july 22 prime minister lawrence wong energy is becoming increasingly central to singapore s economic competitiveness industrial transformation and long-term resilience energy will be a national challenge much like water as the republic continues to power its needs while achieving its net-zero target in view of these priorities tan see leng will devote his full attention to overseeing energy and industry as minister for trade and industry energy and industry tan-soo jie sheng director of the institute for environment and sustainability at the lee kuan yew school of public policy the change formally elevates energy from one of the many issues handled by mti to a central pillar of singapore s economic strategy given that mti already oversees energy the change is more about increasing the political prominence visibility and ministerial ownership of energy he and less about transferring functions fundamentally this is recognition that energy is no longer just a utility sector concern how secure affordable and clean singapore s energy is will shape industrial competitiveness investment attractiveness economic resilience and the feasibility of reaching net-zero he the new name comes at a time of growing geopolitical uncertainty victor nian founding co-chairman of independent think-tank centre for strategic energy and resources for one thing the closure of the strait of hormuz a major global shipping route responsible for 20 per cent of the global oil trade has exposed south-east asia s heavy reliance on imported oil and gas leaving it vulnerable to volatile fuel prices economic disruption and strain on energy systems as the global energy landscape becomes more uncertain integrating energy more explicitly into the ministry s mandate strengthens singapore s ability to pursue decarbonisation while safeguarding energy security he adding that energy security has become a key priority alongside trade and economic competitiveness a more prominent energy portfolio can help provide sustained attention to complex and long-horizon issues such as studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy tan-soo however the name change is ultimately a signal rather than a policy instrument he noted its significance will depend on whether it comes with stronger institutional capabilities clearer accountability better coordination between agencies and sustained investment in energy infrastructure and expertise he pointed out he that energy is an inter-ministry endeavour and coordination with other agencies remains crucial an mti spokesperson the renaming reflects singapore s growing focus on energy which is vital to its economic growth climate goals and national resilience the ministry s core mission has always been to drive growth safeguard and expand our economic space build a future-ready economy and create good jobs and opportunities for singaporeans the spokesperson that remains unchanged a secure affordable and sustainable energy system underpins singapore s attractiveness as a global business hub supports our future industries and enables businesses to innovate grow and invest with confidence the appointment of a full minister to helm energy and industry give energy issues greater weight and allow singapore to pursue the long-term goals more consistently the experts this is crucial as energy decisions in singapore are becoming more complex and time-sensitive madhavi srinivasan executive director of energy research institute ntu citing how the republic is studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy and looking into a regional grid with a full minister and team focusing on energy full-time it enable faster and more strategic long-term decisions she the underlying work was already happening what changes is the institutional weight and continuity behind it which potentially make execution more consistent over the next several years she this is not the first time a change of name has signalled increasing prominence of a portfolio drawing parallels tan-soo the renaming of the ministry of the environment to the ministry of the environment and water resources in 2004 signalled that a resource had become sufficiently important to be placed explicitly in its name adding water resources explicitly recognised water as an existential and strategic national resource he water management was not entirely new to the ministry but naming it elevated its visibility and communicated its long-term importance in 2020 in recognition of sustainability s increasingly important role in the national agenda it was renamed the ministry of sustainability and the environment such changes show how ministry names can evolve with singapore s strategic challenges the change is timely as singapore takes on the asean chairmanship in 2027 experts especially as energy security comes to the fore with energy becoming one of asean s strategic issues singapore as the chair will be in a good position to advance regional initiatives such as the asean power grid cross-border electricity trade and emerging clean energy technologies nian the asean power grid is an interconnected grid that will allow countries in the region where renewable resources are unevenly distributed to trade electricity freely with one another tan-soo noted that many asean countries already have ministers or cabinet-level office-holders with clearly designated responsibility for energy the renaming therefore gives singapore a more visible and readily identifiable counterpart for regional energy diplomacy an mti spokesperson that as singapore prepares to take on the asean chairmanship in 2027 it will continue working closely with asean member states to strengthen regional cooperation including on energy chin hui shan is a journalist covering the environment beat at the straits times ministry of trade and industry

title: Nerf gun bullet, slipper, underwear among litter in machines to collect recyclable bottles, cans
cleaned_text: nerf gun bullet slipper underwear among litter in machines to collect recyclable bottles cans a plastic cup left jamming the opening of a reverse vending machine other inappropriate items found in some machines included an umbrella right and an electronics charging case published aug 07 2026 03 21 pm updated aug 18 2026 05 46 pm singapore an umbrella a nerf gun bullet a slipper and even underwear were among litter found in some of the 1 200 reverse vending machines installed islandwide from april 1 to collect cans and bottles for recycling these acts of mischief can disrupt the machines and cause inconvenience to others wanting to recycle bcrs the operator behind the beverage container return scheme on aug 6 recycling is a shared responsibility and caring for these machines helps keep them accessible and reliable for the community bcrs adding that a plastic cup was found to have jammed the opening of one such machine during a routine check an electronics charging case a paper cup and plastic packaging were found in these return right machines bcrs did not reveal the proportion of litter to the roughly 5 5 million used bottles and cans collected since april 1 a nerf gun bullet found inside a reverse vending machine we do not keep an exact count of every inappropriate item placed in return right machines as these are removed during routine maintenance it under the scheme customers pay an extra 10 cents for each canned or bottled drink but get the money back when they drop the used containers into a return right machine the payments are made directly to customers ez-link cards or dbs paylah wallets during the four months from april to july over one million successful refunds were made for the 5 5 million used bottles and cans dropped off at the machines fifty-five per cent of the materials collected were plastic and 45 per cent were metal some complaints surfaced on social media and reddit from residents who had returned their bottles but did not receive refunds immediately or had their returns rejected by the machines some people even had to e-mail bcrs and wait up to 30 business days to receive their 10-cent deposit some bottles had been rejected as customers did not have physical ez-link cards or dbs paylah wallets to receive their refunds bcrs for example users use their nets flashpay card instead of a physical simplygo ez-link card other refund issues were attributed to connectivity disruptions but the operator did not elaborate on whether they were poor mobile coverage or fibre broadband cuts st has asked bcrs for the number of refund failures a bcrs representative guiding canberra residents in returning their empty drinks bottles at a return right machine on june 6 in july bcrs made some improvements to the machine interface to prevent unsuccessful refunds these include doubling the refund window period to one minute and making the tap for refund button more visible on the screen bcrs we will continue to explore additional e-payment methods we are applying learnings from early operations to improve the return experience reduce avoidable machine errors recalibrate container recognition and acceptance parameters and enhance the refund process these need to be balanced against safeguarding the integrity of the scheme to prevent fraudulent activities where users tamper with the machine to claim over-payments the scheme remains in its transition phase until oct 1 when all bottles and cans in the market must have the 10-cent deposit logo while there are currently 1 200 machines islandwide in community spaces including hdb void decks and supermarkets another 300 machines are expected to be installed in tertiary institutions industrial estates and tourist attractions bcrs is on track to increase the number of return points to around 2 000 by april 2027 the locations of existing machines are found online at the used bottles and cans are sent to a counting and sorting facility in tuas bay before they are later exported to overseas recyclers

title: Dry weather next week could increase haze risk in S’pore if burning worsens in Indonesia: Grace Fu

homes partly due to wildfires in johor published aug 06 2026 12 45 pm updated aug 21 2026 02 19 pm singapore dry weather in the coming week increase the risk of transboundary haze in singapore should burning intensify in kalimantan and southern sumatra minister for sustainability and the environment grace fu on aug 5 in recent days smoke haze has been seen drifting from kalimantan to sarawak but the prevailing winds have not carried the pollutants to singapore the republic is monitoring the situation closely and the government s haze task force is ready to roll out its action plans if air quality is affected by transboundary haze fu in a written reply to a parliamentary question from joan pereira tanjong pagar grc national mask stockpiles are sufficient and schools pre-schools as well as residential and care facilities are equipped with air purifiers she on aug 3 the asean specialised meteorological centre raised its haze alert for the region indicating an escalating risk of transboundary haze as the region has entered the dry south-west monsoon season conditions in 2026 are expected to be drier and warmer than usual due to the development of the el nino climate phenomenon scientists have warned that the el nino grow into a godzilla event with temperatures in the tropical pacific warming rapidly previous severe haze episodes in 1982 1997 and 2015 coincided with super el nino events on the evening of aug 6 the asean centre s website showed widespread hot spots in west kalimantan with scattered hot spots elsewhere in malaysia including sarawak as well as in sumatra java and other parts of kalimantan moderate to dense smoke haze was seen to drift from west kalimantan into the western parts of sarawak moderate to dense smoke plumes were observed in other parts of kalimantan and the southern parts of sumatra hotter and drier conditions make vegetation peatlands and plantations more flammable and fires that start from land clearing or burning waste can spread faster our priority is to protect the health of the public particularly vulnerable groups and to ensure that daily life and essential services can continue as normally as possible fu public communications efforts have been stepped up in view of the heightened risk of haze affecting singapore timely updates on air quality and health advisories will continue in early 2026 singapore title: Singapore to boost defences against animal-borne diseases with six new research projects
cleaned_text: singapore to boost defences against animal-borne diseases with six new research projects the projects will help singapore better anticipate public health risks that can arise from climate change and the cross-border movement of people animals and agents that carry and transmit diseases published aug 05 2026 04 30 pm updated aug 05 2026 09 30 pm singapore amid a surge in pet ownership and human-wildlife interactions the national parks board nparks has awarded grants to projects that investigate how animal-borne diseases spread here announced on aug 5 the projects are funded by the 15 million biosurveillance research programme which taps the local research community to deepen scientific knowledge of animal-borne diseases and develop strategies to manage them led by researchers from duke-nus medical school the national university of singapore nus and nanyang technological university ntu the projects will help the republic better anticipate public health risks that can arise from climate change and the cross-border movement of people animals and agents that carry and transmit diseases nparks six of the seven proposals submitted were selected chua tze hoong group director of veterinary health at nparks animal and veterinary service noted that even as singapore remains free of major animal-borne diseases such as rabies the republic is a major transit hub for migratory birds and animal products and is located in a region with many animal-borne diseases the research supplements singapore s biosurveillance efforts during peacetime chua under the grant researchers will study novel molecular approaches and paint a clearer picture of the complex interactions between disease-carrying organisms humans animals and the environment this includes analysing how land use and human behaviour influence animal movement and disease distribution one project led by gavin smith professor and director of the emerging infectious diseases programme at duke-nus medical school will investigate disease pathways in settings like dog runs veterinary clinics and animal shelters among other things the project will involve sampling the environment for diseases of concern as well as lesser-known bacterial parasites and viruses painting a clearer picture of how they move between humans and animals smith by understanding how diseases spread the authorities can implement simple but effective interventions such as targeted cleaning protocols to reduce the spread of specific disease-causing agents he veterinary consultant teo boon han who is a co-investigator of the project given how close we are with our pets how we hug them kiss them there has been an increase in interest and new evidence regarding the interactions and transmission pathways of certain pathogens from companion animals to humans on a personal note teo who is a managing partner at vettrust singapore the research will help him better protect his veterinary care staff by studying the poorly understood risks that they face on the job another project will assess and quantify the risk of diseases spreading from local wild mammals to humans through shared environments led by janelle thompson an associate professor from ntu s singapore centre for environmental life sciences engineering the team will focus on otters civets plantain squirrels and fruit bats as these are commonly found in urban spaces thompson the team will cast a wide net by measuring biomaterials shed in both nature reserves and high-traffic human-animal interfaces such as housing estates and parks she the point of our project is not to pick one pathogen and focus on it but to use an approach that handle any pathogen the biosurveillance research programme launched in 2025 under singapore s research innovation and enterprise rie 2025 plan is rooted in the world health organization s one health approach the framework recognises the interconnection between human health animal health and the environment singapore s one health agencies nparks the communicable diseases agency the national environment agency the singapore food agency and national water agency pub have operated under a cooperative framework since 2012 the projects will continue to contribute to a better understanding of disease transmission for the agencies allowing nparks to take preventative actions to safeguard public health chua he some of this be in the form of public education we will look at the risk messages that we can share the projects are due to be completed in three years ang qing is a journalist covering local and international breaking news at the straits times with a focus on the environment crime technology and social issues
